widget_guide.copy_hint: the whole guide, for your notes or an AI assistant
widget_guide.lead: A widget is a small Q-App on Home in Qortal Hub and on the widgets screen in Qortal GO. One publish runs in both. It shows one thing at a glance and opens your app for everything else.

look.background: Keep the page background transparent: the host draws the card. Follow the dark and light themes.
look.fast: Show something within about 300 ms: draw the data you kept last time, then refresh. Have an empty state and an error state, never a blank frame or a spinner that doesn't stop.
look.fit: It fills whatever frame it gets, from about 80 × 92 px to a wide card in the Hub. Show fewer items or drop pictures when it's small, use two columns when it's wide. Nothing overflows; only a vertical list may scroll.
look.input: Use buttons and vertical lists, with tap targets at least 40 px tall. No sideways swipes, carousels or long presses: GO uses them to switch screens and arrange widgets.
look.one_job: One job: a number, a short list or the next item. No app bar, menus, tabs, sign-in or splash screen.
look.open: A tap opens your full app at the right place, with `OPEN_NEW_TAB`.
look.title: What a widget looks like

messages.poll: Poll no more often than every 30 s; every few minutes is better for most data.
messages.theme: `THEME_CHANGED` (`theme`) and `LANGUAGE_CHANGED` (`language`): redraw in the new theme or language.
messages.title: Messages from the host
messages.visibility: `GO_WIDGET_VISIBILITY` (`payload.visible`): pause timers, animations and polling while it is `false`, and while `document.visibilityState` is `hidden`.

publish.bundle: Zip the folder with `index.html` at its root. One HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript starts fastest; stay under about 200 KB.
publish.ids: Service `APP`, identifier `go-widget-<slug>`, tag `go-widget`. The Widget option of this form sets all three.
publish.listing: The widget list shows the title, the description and your name's avatar. Keep the title to 24 characters and the description to one sentence.
publish.name: Publish it under your app's name: the Hub keeps `localStorage` per name, so the widget can read what your app saved.
publish.own_app: If your app is already small and fast, it can be its own widget: draw a compact view when the address has `goWidget=1`, and tag the app `go-widget`.
publish.title: Publishing
publish.update: To update it, publish again under the same name and ID. To retire it, publish it again without the `go-widget` tag: it leaves the list, but anyone who added it keeps loading it, so leave a short notice in it.

requests.never: Never: payments, publishing, signing, encryption, chat messages, files, notifications, full screen, pop-ups, and `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt`. A refused request rejects: catch it and keep working.
requests.open: For anything a widget can't do, open your full app at the right page. Use `OPEN_NEW_TAB` with a `qortal://APP/<name>/<path>` link, not `LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE`, which can load the other app inside the widget:
requests.read: Read-only requests that Core answers itself, as in any Q-App: `SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES`, `FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE`, `GET_BALANCE`, `GET_NAME_DATA`, `SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES`, `FETCH_BLOCK` and the like. Feeds need `mode: 'ALL'`.
requests.screen: Only while Home (in GO, the widgets screen) is showing: `OPEN_NEW_TAB`, `SET_TAB`, `OPEN_USER_LOOKUP`, `GET_USER_ACCOUNT` and `GET_WALLET_BALANCE`. The last two ask the user, so ask only after a tap.
requests.title: What a widget may ask for
requests.web: Code and data come only from your bundle, the node and QDN. No outside web services: they may be blocked, and they reveal the user's IP address and activity.

size.ask: Ask once for the size you need. It holds until the user resizes the widget.
size.grid: Rows are 40 px with 12 px gaps, 2 to 14 rows tall. GO has 4 columns, about 79 px each on a phone; the Hub fits as many columns of at least 84 px as it can, so a widget can be much wider than a phone. New widgets are 4 × 5 cells, about 351 to 406 × 248 px.
size.only_widget: `GO_WIDGET_SET_SIZE` and `GO_WIDGET_INFO` answer only inside a widget frame. Send them only when `goWidget=1` is in the address, with a time limit, and never wait for them before drawing.
size.title: Size
size.values: `width` is `'small'` (1 column), `'half'` (2) or `'full'` (4); `height` is in CSS px, rounded up to whole rows.

start.param: `goWidget=1` is always there: draw the widget view from the first frame.
start.request: Call Core's `qortalRequest` by its bare name; `window.qortalRequest` is undefined. In the Hub the widget is the top-level page (`window.parent === window`), in GO an iframe; the same call works in both.
start.storage: `localStorage`: the Hub keeps one per app name, GO one for every Q-App on the node. Start every key with your name.
start.theme: Read `theme` and `lang` from the address when you start. The host's messages are changes after that.
start.title: How it starts

starter.intro: A whole widget, small on purpose: the newest Q-App, in the right theme, paused while hidden, refreshed every few minutes, and opening the app on a tap. Replace `yourname`, the search and `draw` with your own.
starter.title: A starting point

test.tab: Open it as an app with `?goWidget=1&theme=dark`, then `light`, and resize the window from about 80 × 92 px to 830 × 248 px. In a tab nothing answers `GO_WIDGET_*`: it must still draw.
test.title: Testing
test.update: The Hub shows a new version the next time the widget loads (Arrange → Reload); GO within about an hour.
test.widget: After publishing, add it in the Hub (Home → Widgets → Add widget) and in GO (the widgets screen → +). Check theme and language switching, the smallest and largest sizes, that it pauses out of view, and that a tap opens the right page.

tip.any_size: Fit any size, from one small tile to a wide card. Nothing overflows.
tip.first_frame: Draw the widget view from the first frame when the address has `goWidget=1`, on a transparent background.
tip.read_only: Read-only: no payments, publishing or pop-ups. A tap opens your full app with `OPEN_NEW_TAB`.
tip.request: Call Core's `qortalRequest` by its bare name: it works in GO (an iframe) and in the Hub (a top-level page).
tip.theme: Follow `theme` and `lang` from the address, and pause timers and polling while the widget is hidden.
tip.title: Building it as a widget
